title: Lantern framework: compatibility & ergonomics for SDK language support, auth, and streaming
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Problem statement: We receive recurring, high-signal enterprise asks spanning multiple languages for (1) idiomatic client bindings, (2) predictable auth patterns (token rotation, SSO integration in long-lived sessions), and (3) streaming ergonomics (resumable streams, flow-control, cancellation semantics). Current intake is ad-hoc and engineering prioritization is fragmented across language owners. This ticket establishes the 'Lantern' prioritization framework: a repeatable rubric + intake form + quick experiments track to decide what SDK work to take for enterprise vs PLG users.

Scope: Define Lantern framework covering language coverage heuristics, auth contract patterns (short-lived tokens, refresh flows, SSO/OIDC guidance), and streaming API ergonomics (resume semantics, backpressure, reconnect). Deliverables: 1) triage rubric doc, 2) standardized intake template for PM/SE/customer requests, 3) prioritized 12-week roadmap sample with 3 candidate language bindings and 2 auth ergonomics proposals, 4) telemetry plan and customer impact signals.

Acceptance criteria: - A single-page rubric that yields a numeric priority score for requests (customer revenue signal, effort estimate, maintenance cost, security/regulatory needs, platform compatibility). - Intake form deployed in Confluence + intake Slack command. - Three prioritized SDK initiatives (one PLG-friendly, two enterprise-focused) with engineering estimates and owners. - Benchmarks for streaming ergonomics experiment (latency, reconnect time, token refresh success rate) and success thresholds.

Success metrics: - Reduction of triage turnaround to <= 5 business days. - At least 2 enterprise customers approve roadmap items (pilot sign-up) within 8 weeks. - A measurable reduction in support tickets for SDK auth/streaming patterns by 30% after rollouts.

Out-of-scope: Full rewrite of every language binding; deep platform changes that require runtime-1.20 migration. Those will be considered as dependencies if flagged by the rubric.

Key trade-offs considered: - Maintain a thin compatibility shim across languages vs invest in idiomatic libraries per language. Shims reduce maintenance but hurt ergonomics. Lantern will score idiomatic win when customer-revenue *and* usage signals exceed a threshold. - Standardized opinionated auth flow vs support many enterprise-specific token flows. We propose a core recommended pattern (short-lived tokens + refresh callback hook) and an enterprise extension guide.

Stakeholders: PMs (Evelyn Chen, Priya Nair), Engineering leads (Marco Alvarez, Tanya Gorbunov), Design (Liam O'Connor), Security (Rashmi Kapoor), Solutions Eng (Daniel Park).

Links: - PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Lantern+Framework - Intake form prototype: https://forms.redwood.ai/sdkinakein - Slack thread: #sdk-triage (refs: thread: T-8451) - Example customer tickets: CUST-1179, CUST-2013

Open questions: 1) Minimum viable API for resumable streaming (server token refresh handshake or client-led continuation)? 2) Should we support automatic token renewal in SDKs or provide callback hooks only? 3) Level of test coverage / E2E harness per language before GA?
